candidates.title: Prepare recovery checks for agent workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Developers need to add checkpoints, recovery logic, and idempotency handling to agent workflows.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable recovery checklist for one agent workflow, listing checkpoint locations, retry behavior, and operations that must not repeat.
inputs: A list of steps that may fail
A proposed side-effect such as sending a message
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one workflow and asks for a recovery review.
steps: List its steps and mark those with external side effects.
Choose a fictional interruption point and expected restart state.
Draft checkpoint and retry questions for each step.
Flag operations that need an idempotency key or human approval.
Show the checklist for an operator to verify.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A reviewer checks whether every marked side effect has a stated duplicate-prevention or approval rule and whether restart resumes from the chosen point.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer must supply accurate workflow details, inspect the checklist, and design and authorize any real recovery changes. No workflow execution or production modification is included.
unverified: Whether supplied workflow descriptions capture real state
How to model checkpoints for different agent frameworks
Whether any proposed retry is safe or idempotent

ease.reason: A beginner can draft a checklist from a fictional workflow, but the source describes the chore without a tested implementation method.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: agent developers or consultants may pay for recovery reviews; this discussion establishes neither a buyer nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can review fictional workflows and interruption cases; framework-specific correctness remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed tool can organize failure cases and draft checks, while a developer must verify safety and implement recovery.

evidence.reason: The fresh post names checkpoints, recovery logic, and idempotency as developer work but gives no frequency or workflow details.

candidates.reason: Concrete developer chore assessed as a bounded fictional-workflow checklist experiment; provisional mean 4.6 is below the 6 threshold, and no supplied building reference supports implementation.

candidates.title: Draft compact summaries of email threads

demandEvidence.chore: The author describes saving email summaries with a stable reference to the original email and preparing draft context from conversation history.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: To save email resume properly, i need immutable id to reference original email of the resume.

experimentPlan.output: A compact draft summary of a fictional email thread with a stable sample reference and links to the messages represented.
inputs: A list of facts that must be preserved
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a fictional thread and requests a summary.
steps: Keep the supplied synthetic ID attached to the draft.
Extract the main request and relevant prior context.
Draft a short summary without adding unsupported facts.
List source message positions for each retained fact.
Flag ambiguity and send the draft to a human reviewer.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A reviewer compares each summary fact with the fictional messages and confirms the ID points to the intended sample message.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must choose the thread, verify the summary and authorize any use with real email. Use fictional records only; no live mailbox access or identity handling is proposed.
unverified: Whether stable message identifiers are available in a real mailbox
Whether the proposed summary preserves context across varied conversations
Whether email clients permit the desired reference behavior

ease.reason: A beginner can test summaries on fictional threads, but the post gives no attached software capability for email retrieval or stable IDs.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants handling long client email threads might pay for summary drafts; the post establishes a need, not purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week offline prototype can summarize synthetic threads and check traceability; mailbox integration and identifier behavior remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed draft loop can extract and summarize supplied text, but a person must supply, verify, and approve every thread.

evidence.reason: The retained post states a need for stable email references and compact draft context, but gives no frequency or independent corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete bounded task assessed using fictional threads; provisional mean 4.4 is below threshold and there is no supplied implementation reference.
